content.stem: SNT-TC-1A is best described as:
options: A recommended practice for employer-based qualification and certification
A central third-party certification scheme
A legally binding national regulation enforced across all of industry by statute
A weld acceptance standard like API 1104
distractors: SNT-TC-1A is employer-based, not central third-party.
It is a recommended practice, not a regulation.
Acceptance standards are separate documents.
content.explanation: SNT-TC-1A gives guidelines an employer uses to qualify and certify its own NDT personnel.

content.stem: In an employer's written practice, the verb “should” from SNT-TC-1A becomes:
options: “may,” entirely at the employer's option
“shall”
“should,” carried over unchanged
“must,” but only for Level III roles
distractors: The written practice uses shall to make recommendations binding.
Should becomes shall in the employer's written practice.
Shall applies across the written practice, not only to Level III.
content.explanation: SNT-TC-1A uses should for its recommendations; the employer's written practice uses shall to make them binding.

content.stem: Under SNT-TC-1A, NDT personnel are certified by:
options: An independent certification body
ASNT acting directly
The employer
A government inspection agency
distractors: Certification is the employer's responsibility, not a third party's.
ASNT publishes the practice; the employer certifies.
No government body certifies under this practice.
content.explanation: Certification of NDT personnel to all levels is the responsibility of the employer.

content.stem: SNT-TC-1A defines certification as:
options: A passing grade on one written exam
A government-issued occupational license
Membership in a professional society
Written testimony of qualification
distractors: Certification is the written testimony, not a single grade.
It is employer testimony, not a license.
Membership is unrelated to certification here.
content.explanation: SNT-TC-1A defines certification as written testimony of qualification.

content.stem: The certifying agency under SNT-TC-1A is:
options: The employer of the personnel being certified
ASNT as the publishing society
An accredited outside testing laboratory engaged for the work
The national standards body
distractors: The certifying agency is the employer, not ASNT.
An outside agency may supply Level III services, not act as the agency.
No national body is the certifying agency here.
content.explanation: The certifying agency is defined as the employer of the personnel being certified.

content.stem: The certifying authority under SNT-TC-1A is:
options: The candidate's own direct line supervisor, automatically and by default
The person designated in the written practice to sign certifications
Any Level II working in the method
The training instructor of record
distractors: The authority is whoever the written practice designates.
Signing authority is designated, not automatic for a Level II.
The instructor is not, by that role, the certifying authority.
content.explanation: The certifying authority is the person designated in the written practice to sign certifications for the employer.

content.stem: An employer's written practice is reviewed and approved by:
options: An external auditor each year
ASNT's standards council
The employer's NDT Level III
The most senior Level II on staff
distractors: The employer's own Level III reviews and approves it.
ASNT does not approve a given employer's practice.
Approval rests with a Level III, not a Level II.
content.explanation: The written practice is established by the employer and reviewed and approved by the employer's NDT Level III.

content.stem: The written practice governs the control and administration of:
options: Weld acceptance and rejection criteria
Equipment purchasing, calibration intervals, and routine maintenance
Site safety and physical access control
Training, examination, and certification of NDT personnel
distractors: Those live in acceptance standards, not the written practice.
The practice governs personnel, not procurement.
Site safety is outside the written practice's scope.
content.explanation: The employer establishes a written practice for the control and administration of NDT personnel training, examination, and certification.

content.stem: An NDT Level I is qualified to:
options: Perform specific tests and record results under a Level II or III
Interpret and evaluate results against the governing codes and standards alone
Develop and approve the test procedures
Designate the methods and techniques used
distractors: Independent evaluation sits at Level II, not Level I.
Procedure approval is a Level III function.
Designating methods is a Level III function.
content.explanation: A Level I performs specific tests and records results, working under the instruction of a Level II or III.

content.stem: An NDT Level II is qualified to:
options: Establish the company's testing procedures
Set up and calibrate equipment and interpret and evaluate results
Approve the employer's written practice
Work only under the continuous and direct supervision of a Level III at all times
distractors: Establishing procedures is a Level III function.
Approving the practice is a Level III function.
A Level II works without that level of supervision.
content.explanation: A Level II sets up and calibrates equipment and interprets and evaluates results against codes and standards.

content.stem: An NDT Level III is qualified to:
options: Only perform tests under direct supervision
Only record results for later review
Develop, qualify, and approve procedures and interpret codes
Sign certifications yet never develop, qualify, or write procedures
distractors: That describes a Level I, not a Level III.
Recording without evaluation is below Level III.
A Level III does develop and approve procedures.
content.explanation: A Level III develops, qualifies, and approves procedures, interprets codes and standards, and can train and examine personnel.

content.stem: A trainee under SNT-TC-1A:
options: Already hold some limited provisional Level I certificate of their own
Be allowed to certify other trainees
Sign reports after a week of training
Work with a certified individual and not independently interpret
distractors: A trainee is not yet certified at any level.
A trainee certifies no one.
A trainee does not independently report results.
content.explanation: A trainee works with a certified individual and should not independently conduct, interpret, evaluate, or report results.

content.stem: Written qualification examinations under SNT-TC-1A are:
options: Closed-book, except for data supplied with the exam
Fully open-book in every case
Open only to Level III candidates
Replaced entirely by a structured oral interview instead
distractors: Written exams are closed-book apart from supplied data.
The closed-book rule applies to all levels.
Written exams are not replaced by an interview.
content.explanation: Written examinations are closed-book, except that necessary data such as tables may be provided with the exam.

content.stem: The composite grade for Level I or II is:
options: The lowest of the three exam scores
The simple average of the general, specific, and practical exams
The practical examination score alone
A weighted average that strongly favors the specific examination result
distractors: It is the simple average, not the minimum.
All three parts feed the composite.
The average is simple, not weighted.
content.explanation: For Level I and II, the composite grade is the simple average of the general, specific, and practical results.

content.stem: To pass, a candidate needs a composite of at least 80% and:
options: No exam part below 80% at all
A perfect score on the practical
No individual written exam below 70%
At least 90% achieved on the specific examination
distractors: The written floor is 70%, with an 80% composite.
No perfect score is required.
No 90% threshold applies to the specific exam.
content.explanation: Passing requires a composite of at least 80%, with no individual written exam below 70% and a practical of at least 80%.

content.stem: The practical examination must reach a grade of at least:
distractors: The written floor is 70%; the practical floor is 80%.
60% is below any passing threshold here.
90% is higher than the required practical minimum.
content.explanation: The practical examination should have a passing grade of at least 80%.

content.stem: A candidate who fails must wait before reexamination at least:
options: 30 days, or take suitable additional training
7 days only, with no additional training option at all
6 months, in all cases
1 full year before any retry
distractors: The wait is at least 30 days, not 7.
The minimum wait is 30 days, not six months.
A year overstates the minimum wait.
content.explanation: Those failing should wait at least 30 days, or take suitable additional training as the Level III determines, before reexamination.

content.stem: An examination may not be administered by:
options: A qualified Level III examiner
Oneself or a subordinate
An approved outside agency
A trained Level III designee
distractors: A Level III may administer exams; a subordinate may not.
An outside agency may provide exam services.
A designated, trained representative may administer exams.
content.explanation: In no case shall an examination be administered by oneself or by a subordinate.

content.stem: Recommended exam question content is drawn from:
options: The API 1104 acceptance section
The ASME boiler and pressure vessel code
The ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines
The employer's equipment purchase records
distractors: Acceptance criteria are not the source of exam topics.
ASME is not the topical-outline source here.
Purchase records are unrelated to exam content.
content.explanation: Recommended training outlines and references for examination content are in ANSI/ASNT CP-105.

content.stem: Near-vision acuity must allow reading Jaeger No. 2 at:
options: Not less than 36 in, checked once every five years
Any distance, checked once at hire
Exactly 8 in, checked every month
Not less than 12 in (30.5 cm), checked annually
distractors: Near vision is at 12 in and checked annually.
A set distance and annual check apply.
The distance is not less than 12 in, checked yearly.
content.explanation: Near-vision acuity should allow reading Jaeger No. 2 at not less than 12 in (30.5 cm), administered annually.

content.stem: Color-contrast differentiation is verified:
options: At initial certification and every five years
Only once, at initial certification
Every single month alongside the near-vision test
Only for Level III personnel
distractors: Color vision is rechecked at five-year intervals.
Color vision follows a five-year cycle, not monthly.
Color vision applies regardless of level.
content.explanation: Color-contrast differentiation is demonstrated at initial certification and at five-year intervals thereafter.

content.stem: Pharmacological agents such as eye drops to improve acuity are:
options: Allowed at the candidate's discretion
Not permitted for the vision test
Required before every test
Allowed only for Level III candidates
distractors: Acuity-improving drops are not allowed for the test.
They are prohibited, not required.
They are not permitted for any candidate.
content.explanation: Eye drops or agents that temporarily improve visual acuity shall not be used for the examination.

content.stem: Certification begins on the date that:
options: The candidate finishes and passes the final written examination
The training course is completed
The Certifying Authority signs the certification record
The application is first submitted
distractors: Certification dates from the signing, not the last exam.
Course completion does not start certification.
Submission does not start certification.
content.explanation: The date of certification is the date the Certifying Authority signs the certification record.

content.stem: The recommended maximum recertification interval is:
options: Three years
Ten years
Two years
Five years
distractors: The recommended maximum interval is five years.
Ten years exceeds the recommended interval.
Two years is shorter than the recommended interval.
content.explanation: The recommended maximum recertification interval is five years for all levels.

content.stem: After termination, a new employer may certify a person to the former level on examination within:
options: Six months
One month
Two years
Five years
distractors: The window is six months, not one.
Two years is longer than the six-month window.
Five years far exceeds the window.
content.explanation: A terminated certificate holder may be certified to the former level by a new employer on examination within six months.

content.stem: Reinstatement without a new examination is allowed within six months if:
options: The person simply asks the new employer in writing to be reinstated
The records were kept and the certificate had not expired
A Level II vouches for them verbally
The new employer waives the records
distractors: Reinstatement needs kept records and an unexpired certificate.
A verbal vouch does not satisfy the conditions.
The records condition cannot be waived for reinstatement.
content.explanation: Reinstatement without a new exam is allowed within six months if records were maintained and the certificate had not expired.

content.stem: Personnel certification records are kept by:
options: ASNT, on a central registry
The certified individual alone
The employer, for the period set in the written practice
The responsible Level III, kept in their own personal working file
distractors: Records are held by the employer, not centrally by ASNT.
The employer maintains the records.
Records are the employer's, kept on file.
content.explanation: Personnel certification records are maintained by the employer for the duration specified in the written practice.

content.stem: The ASNT Level III Basic examination's questions on understanding the SNT-TC-1A document number:
options: Forty-five
Five
Zero
Fifteen
distractors: Fifteen questions cover the SNT-TC-1A document on the Basic exam.
The Basic exam allots fifteen, not five, on the document.
The Basic exam does include document questions.
content.explanation: The Level III Basic examination includes fifteen questions on understanding the SNT-TC-1A document.

content.stem: The Level III method examination's questions on fundamentals and principles number:
options: Thirty
Fifteen
Twenty
Forty
distractors: Fifteen is the application-and-procedures count, not fundamentals.
Twenty is the codes-interpretation count, not fundamentals.
Forty overstates the fundamentals count.
content.explanation: The Level III method examination includes thirty questions on fundamentals and principles for each method.

content.stem: A valid ASNT NDT Level III or ASNT 9712 certificate may:
options: Replace the employer's certification outright
Fulfill exam criteria if the Level III finds it meets the written practice
Be disregarded by the employer
Automatically certify the holder at any company without any employer review at all
distractors: It can fulfill exam criteria, not replace certification.
A valid certificate may be accepted, not ignored.
Acceptance is at the engaging employer's Level III discretion.
content.explanation: A valid ASNT NDT Level III or ASNT 9712 certificate may fulfill exam criteria if the Level III finds the exams meet the written practice.

content.stem: An outside agency under SNT-TC-1A provides:
options: Government inspection of the employer
Certification that is entirely independent of any employer involvement
NDT Level III services reviewed by the engaging employer
Free training offered to all candidates
distractors: An outside agency supplies Level III services, not inspection.
Its qualifications are reviewed by the engaging employer.
An outside agency is not a free training provider.
content.explanation: An outside agency provides NDT Level III services whose qualifications the engaging employer has reviewed.

content.stem: A recommended practice, in SNT-TC-1A's own terms, is:
options: A mandatory rule enforced directly by ASNT upon every single employer
A contract between purchaser and supplier
A method acceptance standard for welds
Guidelines to assist the employer in setting up its program
distractors: It is guidance, not an ASNT-enforced mandate.
It is a recommended practice, not a contract.
Acceptance standards are separate documents.
content.explanation: A recommended practice is a set of guidelines to assist the employer in developing procedures for its specific requirements.
